div.head: Lib Lond 1
div.ab: Sciendum est enim, quod infra III. miliarii spacium ex omni parte extra ciuitatem Londoniarum non debet homo alterum retinere uel inpedire nec etiam cum eo mercatum agere, si in pace ciuitatis ad eam uenire uoluerit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 673 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s heading: [Libertas Londoniensis.]

Vgl. Gl London 34a. 38; Handel 16a; s. u. 9, 1. Eine privilegierte Leuga von drei Meilen Durchmesser umgibt Battle um 1115; Davis EHR 1914, 427.—Das Gewerbe wird in einem bestimmten Umkreis um eine Stadt herum gebannt in Freibriefen 12. Jhs.; Ballard Brit. bor. char. 168

Cf. Gl London 34a. 38; Handel 16a; see below 9, 1. A privileged Leuga three miles in diameter surrounds Battle c. 1115; Davis EHR 1914, 427.—In charters of the 12th cent. trade is banned within a fixed radius around a town; Ballard Brit. bor. char. 168

div.ab: For it is to be known that within the space of three miles on every side outside the city of London a man ought not to detain or hinder another, nor even trade with him, if he wishes to come to it in the peace of the city.
